build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player character runs and jumps with tight, responsive controls. Movement is frame-precise with no input lag. The character can change direction mid-air. Score 0 if movement is sluggish, unresponsive, or absent.

Hazards (spinning saw blades, spikes, retracting obstacles) kill the player instantly on contact. Respawn is near-instantaneous with no loading screen or menu — death and retry form a seamless sub-second loop. Score 0 if hazards do not kill or respawn requires menu interaction.

A replay ghost of the best successful run plays back as a translucent afterimage when re-entering a cleared level. The ghost follows the exact path and timing of the recorded run. Score 0 if no ghost replay system exists.

Each level is a single screen with a clear start point and goal. Reaching the goal completes the level and records completion time. The level-select grid shows completion status. Score 0 if levels have no clear goal or completion state.
A global death counter persists across the entire game and is visible on the level-select screen. Per-level completion times are tracked and displayed. Score 0 if no tracking exists.

At least 20 distinct levels are present across multiple worlds, with unique layouts that test different platforming skills. Levels within a world share a theme but vary in structure. Score 0 if fewer than 10 levels exist or all share identical layouts.

At least 3 distinct hazard types are present (saw blades, spikes, retracting platforms, crumbling blocks, moving obstacles) each with different timing and avoidance patterns. Score 0 if only one hazard type exists.
Multiple worlds (at least 3) with distinct visual themes and new hazard introductions. Completing all levels in a world unlocks the next. Score 0 if only one world exists.

Difficulty escalates clearly within and across worlds — early levels teach mechanics gently, later levels demand precise timing and complex sequences. The final levels in each world are noticeably harder. Score 0 if difficulty is flat or random.
A world-completion or game-completion results screen shows total deaths, total time, and per-level best times. Results reflect actual gameplay performance. Score 0 if no results exist.
A styled title screen shows the game name, a level-select grid, and the global death counter before gameplay begins. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.

The game flow connects title -> level select -> gameplay -> level complete -> back to select without restarting. All transitions are smooth and reachable through in-game UI. Score 0 if transitions are missing or require relaunch.
During gameplay, the current level timer, death flash feedback, and goal indicator are clearly visible without obstructing the play area. Score 0 if no gameplay feedback is visible.

Readability at 1280x720 is strong: player, hazards, platforms, goal, and background layers are all clearly distinguishable. Saw blades look different from spikes which look different from safe platforms. Score 0 if elements blend together.

The art direction is coherent across title, levels, hazards, character, ghost, and UI — a consistent speed-platformer aesthetic with bold contrast and unified palette. Score 0 if mostly default UI or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

Level environments use real sprite or tile art for platforms, hazards, backgrounds, and the player character — not plain ColorRect fills. Different worlds have visually distinct themes. Score 0 if environments are uniform color fills.
HUD and UI chrome: level select grid, death counter, timer, completion screens use styled themed widgets — not raw unstyled HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if primary UI elements are obviously unstyled.

Animation and feedback: death produces a burst or shake, the ghost has a translucent trail effect, saw blades spin visibly, and level completion has a celebratory animation. Score 0 if all state changes snap silently.
